claims.text: Differences in mechanical properties among the quinary alloy and its FCC quaternary and ternary derivatives arise partly from altered stacking-fault energies.
Differences in mechanical properties among these alloys arise partly from the evolution of short-range chemical order.
The equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloy has an intermediate stacking-fault energy relative to its quaternary and ternary derivatives.
An intermediate stacking-fault energy optimizes the balance between deformation twinning and dislocation slip in the quinary alloy.
The quinary alloy contains heterogeneous short-range-order clusters.
Heterogeneous short-range-order clusters impede dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion from short-range order enhances strain hardening and delays strain localization.
Removing elements from the quinary alloy eliminates key atomic interactions and shifts the stacking-fault energy of the resulting quaternary or ternary alloys away from an optimal intermediate range.
Stacking-fault energies outside the proposed intermediate range produce predominantly planar slip or excessive deformation twinning.
The quaternary and ternary derivatives have more homogeneous or absent short-range order compared with the quinary alloy.
More homogeneous or absent short-range order in the derivative alloys causes reduced strain hardening and earlier strain localization.
Relative to the quinary baseline, the quaternary and ternary alloys will have lower yield strength.
Relative to the quinary baseline, the quaternary and ternary alloys will have lower strain-hardening rates.
Relative to the quinary baseline, the quaternary and ternary alloys will localize strain earlier.
Twin density, partial-dislocation spacing, and dislocation dynamics can serve as indirect measures of stacking-fault energy.
High-resolution atom-probe tomography can quantify the proposed short-range-order patterns and their heterogeneity.
Identical thermomechanical processing will maintain sufficiently similar initial microstructures to isolate the effects of composition on stacking-fault energy and short-range order.
